RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 10

That number is a tentative subjective estimate, not a measured probability; the available facts don’t support a reliable calculation.

An all-male panel isn’t, by itself, evidence that sex influenced the decision—particularly where you and the appointee are both men. It could nevertheless raise a procedural issue if university rules require gender-balanced panels.

Your stronger next step is to follow up in writing, requesting the selection criteria, their weighting, and feedback on your assessment. More publications and a completed PhD don’t automatically outweigh relevant industry experience, unless the advertised requirements say otherwise.

Check recruitment policies and appeal deadlines now. Raise panel composition as a compliance question, not an allegation of discrimination.
